contentHtml:
ETHIOPIA—The Regionalized Vaccine Manufacturing Collaborative (RVMC) has launched its 2028–2032 strategy at the fifth International Conference on Public Health in Africa (CPHIA 2026) to strengthen regional vaccine production and improve access to vaccines across emerging markets.

The five-year roadmap outlines four strategic initiatives aimed at addressing the political, regulatory, financial, and market challenges limiting the sustainability of regional vaccine manufacturing.

It also signals a shift in RVMC’s approach, from building evidence and consensus to supporting governments, regional organisations and manufacturers in implementing practical solutions.

Regional manufacturing capacity remains limited

Despite investments in production facilities and manufacturing capacity, regional suppliers continue to meet a small proportion of vaccine demand.

RVMC’s ecosystem status report, Towards Regionalized Vaccine Manufacturing, found that in 2023, regional manufacturers supplied just 1% of vaccine demand in Africa, compared with 25% in Latin America and the Caribbean and 29% in Southeast Asia.

Only three regional manufacturers were producing at least five vaccines at commercial scale, and none was based in Africa.

The findings highlight the need for supportive government policies, efficient regulatory systems and predictable markets.

Manufacturers also require sufficient operational capacity to meet routine healthcare needs while scaling up production during public health emergencies.

“Progress is real, but uneven, and factories alone cannot deliver health security,” said Dr Frederik Kristensen, Managing Director of RVMC.

He noted that the next phase would focus on coordinating governments, regulators, manufacturers and investors to build financially sustainable production systems that serve regional markets and contribute to global health security.

Four initiatives backed by US$35 million

RVMC has allocated US$35 million to implement four interconnected initiatives under its new strategy.

The Insights Initiative will strengthen the evidence base by consolidating manufacturing and market data to support investment and policy decisions.

The Regional Pathways Initiative will help regions develop investment-ready manufacturing plans aligned with their priorities.

Meanwhile, the Collaborative Support Initiative will provide technical and advisory assistance to governments, manufacturers and funders to reduce investment risks.

The Inter-regional Cooperation Initiative will facilitate collaboration across Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Southeast Asia, including joint efforts to address shared manufacturing challenges and expand market opportunities.

Speaking at CPHIA 2026, Dr Jean Kaseya, Director-General of Africa CDC and an RVMC Executive Committee member, highlighted Africa’s ambition to produce 60% of its vaccine requirements locally by 2040.

He identified manufacturing capacity, reliable markets, technology transfer and appropriate financing as essential to achieving the target.

He also pointed to the Partnership for African Health and Medical Manufacturing (PHAHM) as a platform for working with African countries and partners to establish these conditions.

Dr Richard Hatchett, Chief Executive Officer of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), which hosts the RVMC Secretariat, said the strategy would build on existing efforts to strengthen regional manufacturing systems.

He emphasised that routine production and reliable market intelligence are essential for maintaining manufacturing capabilities and ensuring equitable vaccine distribution during outbreaks.

Ahead of the 2028 implementation period, RVMC will continue its ongoing activities while working with regional partners to establish priorities, implementation plans and performance measures for the new strategy.
